title: Effective and Scalable Math Support: Experimental Evidence on the Impact of an AI- Math Tutor in Ghana
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an AI-powered math tutor delivered through WhatsApp can improve students’ mathematics learning in a low-resource educational context. The authors focus on the challenge that many students in sub-Saharan Africa receive instruction that is not well matched to their skill level and have limited access to individualized tutoring. The study asks whether a low-cost, scalable mobile tutoring tool can provide meaningful learning gains when added to ordinary schooling.

The intervention studied is Rori, an AI-based conversational math tutor developed by Rising Academies. Rori provides students with micro-lessons, scaffolded practice, hints, worked solutions, and natural-language interaction via WhatsApp on basic mobile phones. In the study, treatment schools received access to Rori for two 30-minute sessions per week during study hall, while control schools continued normal schooling without Rori. Students in both groups took the same mathematics assessment at baseline and endline over an approximately 8-month period in 2023.

The population consisted of students in Rising Academies schools in Ghana, primarily grades 3-8 in the participation section, though the paper also describes grades 3-9 in the introduction. Eleven schools were included, with school-level random assignment to treatment or control. A total of 637 students completed the baseline assessment and 477 completed both baseline and endline. Teachers were present during Rori sessions mainly to address technical issues, while students used the system independently.

The main finding is that students in the treatment group showed significantly greater growth in math scores than those in the control group. The treatment group’s average growth exceeded the control group by 3.01 points, with p < 0.001, and the reported effect size was 0.36, which the authors interpret as moderate to large in education research and potentially comparable to about an extra year of learning. The paper concludes that AI-supported, chat-based tutoring on low-cost mobile infrastructure may be a cost-effective and scalable way to improve math outcomes in LMIC settings, while noting that results are preliminary, based on year 1 only, and should be interpreted cautiously.

identified_tools.name: Rori
identified_tools.description: An AI-powered math tutor delivered through WhatsApp that provides a curriculum of micro-lessons, scaffolded practice questions, hints, worked solutions, and natural-language chat using NLP/LLM methods.
identified_tools.use_case: Students in grades 3-8/9 in Ghanaian schools used Rori independently during study hall for two 30-minute sessions per week over 8 months as supplemental math instruction alongside normal classes.

findings.finding_summary: Students with access to Rori showed significantly higher math growth than controls on a 35-item math assessment administered at baseline and endline over 8 months. Control students had mean growth of 2.12 (SD = 6.30, N=241) versus 5.13 (SD = 7.03, N=237/236 reported inconsistently) in treatment, a 3.01-point difference with p < 0.001; the reported effect size was Cohen's d = 0.36.
findings.measure: Growth in raw scores on a 35-question math assessment covering numeracy and algebra skills from grades 3 to 5 on the Global Proficiency Framework

quality_tier_rationale: This is an experimental school-level study with random assignment of 11 schools to treatment and control and baseline equivalence checks, but it is a preliminary year-1 evaluation with attrition and some reporting inconsistencies in sample counts, so it falls short of blue-tier certainty.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effect size for math outcomes was d = 0.36, which exceeds the 0.20 threshold for medium/large impact under the framework.
